evidence.note: Front-loads the cheap-but-fatal vendoring gate: curl -fsSL of the three exact unpkg URLs into /app/static/ at the correct flat paths at build time (offline serving), rather than CDN at runtime.
Recomputes sha256sum of all three vendored libs right after first boot — verifying the hash-pin gate is actually satisfied instead of assuming.
find scan for package.json/lockfiles/vite configs — proactively auditing the no-build-tool anti-cheat gate.
Dumps response headers and greps for unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval — concrete check of the strict CSP gate.
Re-runs sha256sum late (regression guard), plus find/du/__pycache__ cleanup auditing for large-binary and stray-artifact anti-cheat gates as the build evolved.
Checks seeded public-timeline content and counts (seed-minimum gate) and UTF-8 punctuation rendering.

reasoning: The agent explicitly targets and verifies most kill-switch gates with concrete checks — vendoring pristine downloads to exact paths early (step 16), recomputing hashes twice (33, 86, guarding against regression), scanning for build-tool artifacts and large binaries (66, 89-92), inspecting the strict CSP (85), and checking seed minimums (94-95). This matches the level-8 anchor of triaging the cheap-but-fatal set and verifying each rather than assuming. It falls short of 10 because there is no visible brand/purple-palette measurement, no canary-strip caveat on the hash checks, and no explicit offline-runtime confirmation, so the enumeration is not fully exhaustive.
